requirements_summary: Workload types: low-latency chat for traders, high-throughput embeddings/reranking for compliance search.
Latency SLO: p95 < 30ms for embeddings, p99 < 100ms for chat during market hours; tail guarantees requested.
Throughput: sustained 2.5k reqs/s for reranking pipeline; burst to 10k reqs/s for end-of-day jobs.
Reserved GPU planning: target reserved pool equivalent to 8xA100 (or 16xA30) with autoscale/burst policy; want clear failover to warm standby.
SLA asks: uptime >=99.99%, detailed credit schedule per % drop, attribution by region, exclusion windows for scheduled maintenance with 48h notice.
Support: P1 response <=15m, P2 <=1h, 24/7 phone escalation; dedicated TAM preferred.
Security: SSO/SAML, KMS integration, audit logs retention 7 years, EU data residency for subset of workloads.
Contracting: prefer 12–24 month committed reserved capacity with quarterly reviews and unit pricing for burst usage.
sla_requirements: Uptime target: Atlas requests 99.99% annual uptime for Dedicated cluster used for trading signals
Credit schedule: pro-rata credits tied to downtime buckets (>=0.1% <0.5% = 10% credit, >=0.5% <1% = 25%, >1% escalate) — Atlas wants stronger top-end credits
Maintenance windows: preferred outside market hours (US Eastern 18:00-04:00), 48h notice for scheduled maintenance; Redwood standard monthly window needs adjustment
Support response times: P1 <=15 minutes (on-call), P2 <=1 hour; require phone escalation and named on-call TAM
Measurement: SLA measured per-region and per-dedicated-cluster; Atlas requires transparency (metrics + dashboards) and monthly SLA report
Throughput guarantees: quantifiable throughput per reserved GPU type with defined degradation policies and failover to standby capacity
Reserved GPU billing: fixed commit for reserved pool + overage/burst pricing; want caps on burst cost and predictable unit economics
